rows.grounds: compound of kiñcit and kālaṃ in accusative singular masculine

items.question: How should the guru bestow the mantra after arranging matters?
premises: guru arranges matters for some time
guru bestows mantra to own disciple
items.inference: The guru first arranges matters, then bestows the mantra to his own disciple.
uncertainties: exact duration of kiñcit+kālaṃ is unspecified
items.plain_english: After arranging matters for some time, the guru should bestow the mantra to his own disciple.

items.question: What result is promised at the end of the body?
premises: at end of body eternal liberation
items.inference: At the end of the body there is eternal liberation, as spoken by Śaṅkara.
uncertainties: whether dehānte means death or final bodily state
items.plain_english: At the end of the body there is eternal liberation, so Śaṅkara has spoken.

items.question: What should the guru always maintain for the dear one?
premises: guru should always make tradition unbroken
guru is the agent of continuity
items.inference: The guru should always keep the tradition unbroken, O dear one.
uncertainties: whether priye addresses Pārvatī or disciple
items.plain_english: O dear one, the guru should always keep the tradition unbroken.
